name: en seminar: ML in production
transcript: Today I want to talk about why machine learning projects fail after the prototype.
The first reason is data drift. The data you trained on stops looking like the data you see in production.
The second reason is that nobody owns the model once it ships. There is no on-call rotation for it.
Third, evaluation. Teams measure accuracy on a test set, but never measure business impact.
A good practice is to monitor the input distribution and set alerts when it shifts.
Another practice is to keep a small human-reviewed sample every week.
Let me give an example. A retailer's demand model lost thirty percent accuracy in two months after a holiday season.
To summarise: watch for drift, assign an owner, and measure impact, not just accuracy.
Questions? Yes, how often should you retrain?
It depends on how fast your data changes. I don't have a universal number, and I'd be suspicious of anyone who does.
